title: GHG Protocol scopes and boundaries
facts: Scope 1 = direct emissions from owned/controlled sources; Scope 2 = purchased energy; Scope 3 = all other value-chain emissions across 15 defined categories.
Organisational boundary uses either equity share or control (financial or operational) — the choice must be documented and applied consistently.
Scope 2 dual reporting: both location-based (grid average) and market-based (contractual instruments) figures are required by the Scope 2 Guidance.

title: The 15 Scope 3 categories
facts: Upstream: 1 purchased goods & services, 2 capital goods, 3 fuel & energy related, 4 upstream transport, 5 waste, 6 business travel, 7 commuting, 8 upstream leased assets.
Downstream: 9 downstream transport, 10 processing of sold products, 11 use of sold products, 12 end-of-life, 13 downstream leased assets, 14 franchises, 15 investments (financed emissions).
For most financial institutions, category 15 dominates — often >95% of total footprint.

title: PCAF financed emissions methodology
facts: PCAF attribution: financed emissions = (outstanding amount ÷ EVIC or total equity+debt) × borrower/investee emissions.
Data quality scores run 1 (audited, reported emissions) to 5 (economic-activity proxies); portfolios disclose an exposure-weighted average score.
PCAF Standard v2 (2022) covers seven asset classes including listed equity, business loans, project finance, mortgages, commercial real estate and sovereign debt.

title: India grid emission factor
facts: India's Central Electricity Authority publishes the national grid emission factor in its CO2 Baseline Database; the weighted average (combined margin) has been around 0.71–0.73 tCO2/MWh in recent editions.
Use the CEA factor for location-based Scope 2 in India; RECs or green tariffs support a lower market-based figure.

title: GWP values (IPCC AR6, 100-year)
facts: Common refrigerants: R-410A ≈ 2,088, R-134a ≈ 1,430, R-32 ≈ 675, R-404A ≈ 3,922 — a small leak of R-404A outweighs tonnes of CO2.
IFRS S2 and most regulators now expect AR5 or AR6 GWP sets, stated explicitly in the methodology note.

title: Common emission factors (DEFRA 2024)
facts: Diesel ≈ 2.68 kgCO2e/litre; petrol ≈ 2.31 kgCO2e/litre; natural gas ≈ 56.1 kgCO2e/GJ (≈2.04 kg/m³).
Average economy long-haul flight ≈ 0.15–0.20 kgCO2e per passenger-km including radiative forcing; UK DEFRA publishes updated factors every June.
Landfilled mixed municipal waste ≈ 0.45–0.6 tCO2e per tonne depending on composition.

title: SBTi reduction pathways
facts: SBTi's cross-sector 1.5°C pathway requires a minimum 4.2% absolute reduction per year for Scope 1+2 near-term targets.
Scope 3 targets are required when Scope 3 is ≥40% of total emissions; near-term Scope 3 ambition minimum is well-below-2°C (≈2.5%/yr).
The Net-Zero Standard requires 90–95% absolute reduction by 2050 with residual emissions neutralised by permanent removals.

title: Case study — Mahindra Group carbon programme
facts: Mahindra & Mahindra committed to carbon neutrality by 2040, was an early Indian adopter of an internal carbon price (US$10/t announced 2016), and multiple group companies carry validated SBTi targets.
Its EP100/RE100 memberships pair energy-productivity doubling with renewable procurement — a common pattern for Indian conglomerate inventories.

title: Verification and audit-trail expectations
facts: Verifiers (ISAE 3410 / ISSA 5000) trace each inventory line to: activity data source, emission factor + vintage, calculation, and responsible owner.
Classic findings: stale emission factors (3+ years old), unit errors (GJ vs MWh), market-based claims without retired certificates, and double counting across scopes.
Keep a base-year recalculation policy — structural changes (M&A, divestment, methodology) above a threshold (commonly 5%) trigger restatement.

title: Case study — Infosys carbon neutrality
facts: Infosys declared carbon neutrality from FY2020 (PAS 2060), combining on-site solar, RE procurement and community-based offset projects covering Scope 1–3.
Its published ESG data book itemises emissions by scope and category with third-party assurance — a strong reference for IT-services inventories.
